The '''2016–17 Ligue 1''' season was the 79th season since its establishment. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the defending champions. The fixtures were announced on 1 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/season-2016-2017-calendar.htm |title=The LFP has ratified the Ligue 1 calendar for season 2016–17 – check out the key dates! |website=www.ligue1.com |date=1 June 2016 |access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref> The season began on 12 August 2016 and ended on 20 May 2017.

On 17 May 2017, [[AS Monaco FC| Monaco]] secured the title after 37 matches, their first since the [[1999–2000 French Division 1|1999–2000]] season, the first under the Ligue 1 name and their eighth French title in total.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.espnfc.com/as-monaco/story/3128518/monacos-ligue-1-title-worth-four-of-paris-saint-germains-leonardo-jardim|title=Prince Albert II, boss Leonardo Jardim hail Monaco's Ligue 1 title|date=17 May 2017|work=ESPN|access-date=18 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39909535|title=Monaco 2 St Etienne 0|date=17 May 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=18 May 2017}}</ref>

==Teams==
There were 20 clubs in the league, with three promoted teams from [[2015–16 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]] replacing the three teams that were relegated from [[2015–16 Ligue 1|Ligue 1]] following the [[2015–16 in French football|2015–16 season]]. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.

==Relegation play-offs==
The 2016–17 season saw the return of [[Ligue 1 relegation/promotion play-offs|relegation play-offs]] between the 18th placed Ligue 1 team, [[FC Lorient|Lorient]], and the 3rd placed [[2016–17 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]] team, [[Troyes AC|Troyes]], on a two-legged confrontation.
